source.title: Deep Exploration of Epoch-wise Double Descent in Noisy Data: Signal Separation, Large Activation, and Benign Overfitting
source.authors: Tomoki Kubo; Ryuken Uda; Yusuke Iida

page_placements.theme: Clean and noisy feature learning during the second descent

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test-loss trajectories over epochs in three MLPs, directly testing epoch-wise double descent, but in a different model setup.
record.gate_note: The study explicitly reports test-loss trajectories for MLP7, MLP5, and MLP3. Results cited from other studies are not included. The analyses of internal signal separation and large activations are not rows because they do not measure a versioned claim outcome.
record.test_reason: The study trains three fully connected MLPs on CIFAR-10 with 30% label noise, following Nakkiran et al.'s setup. It reports whether test loss follows a fall-rise-fall shape over epochs, which bears directly on V2. It uses a different architecture class (MLPs rather than ResNets or CNNs) and test loss rather than test error.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors report epoch-wise double descent only in MLP7, with MLP5 and MLP3 matching Nakkiran's intermediate and small regimes. They interpret the second descent as a benign-overfitting state. They propose that clean and noisy signal separation plus a shallow-layer large activation compressing inputs explain it.
record.recipe_differences: The study says it follows Nakkiran et al.'s CIFAR-10 setup, including 30% label noise, but tests fully connected MLPs and focuses on epoch-wise loss curves and internal representations rather than reproducing all original settings or axes.
record.method_sensitivity: The epoch-wise double-descent outcome differed by model: it was reported for MLP7 but not MLP5 or MLP3.

fits_no_version.finding: In MLP7 and MLP5, hidden-layer activations for clean and noisy training data separate over training, more strongly in deeper layers. In MLP7, a single large activation in a shallow layer emerges at about the onset of the second descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-wise double descent under label noise coincides with internal separation of clean and noisy signals and with the emergence of a large activation (a mechanistic correlate, not a rate of the behaviour).

record.problems: Only three MLP architectures are tested on one dataset and one label-noise level. The epoch-wise claim is reported for only one model. The relevant test-loss values are described qualitatively rather than reported numerically.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep. The three MLPs differ in depth and width, but test error is not traced against size around an interpolation threshold.
Not tested on other datasets, noise levels, optimizers or architectures. Test error/accuracy is not reported as the outcome; only test loss is discussed.
No non-deep model classes and no capacity sweep.
No effective-complexity measure is computed or used to predict where the peak falls.
Label noise is held fixed at 30%. Regularization is not varied and multiple peaks are not examined.
No re-expression in terms of an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Test accuracy curves (Fig. 1 A–C) are plotted but no row records whether test accuracy/error, the original's measure, shows the same double-descent shape.
Training budgets differ: MLP7 ran 10^5 epochs while MLP5 and MLP3 ran 10^6. MLP7's second descent begins before training data are fully fitted.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' label for MLP5 and MLP3 is replaced with limits_scope. The original source itself reports that epoch-wise double descent appears mainly in large models, and the authors present the smaller models' behaviour as consistent with that. The absence is therefore a size condition on V2, not evidence against it. Uncertainty is not reported for the loss curves (single runs; error bars appear only on similarity and activation plots), so the record's uncertainty_reported 'y' is doubtful. There are no numeric loss values, only qualitative text.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep testing test error as model size grows.
Tests test loss over epochs for three MLPs on CIFAR-10 with 30% label noise; does not establish the pattern across other datasets, noise levels, or training setups.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison across model classes testing a general capacity-risk curve.
Does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
Uses one label-noise setting and does not vary noise or regularization, test for multiple peaks, or tune regularization optimally.
Does not re-express the curve using an effective parameter count.

rows.subject: MLP7
rows.size_stated: Six hidden layers with 2048, 2048, 1024, 1024, 512, and 512 neurons; output layer with 10 neurons.
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated test loss over training epochs.
rows.value: The paper reports epoch-wise double descent; test loss began decreasing again after around 7,000 epochs.
rows.note: The paper describes an earlier increase in test loss followed by the later decrease. Numeric curve values are not stated.
rows.check: The row is broadly correct. Test loss rose from about 100 to 7,000 epochs as noisy labels were fitted, then fell again after about 7,000 epochs, out to 10^5 epochs. The measure is test loss, not the test error used by the version and the original. The text also cites 'Fig. 1 A', an accuracy panel, though the loss panel is D.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2; Section 3, Figure 1 caption and accompanying paragraphs: MLP7 test loss increases during epochs 100–7,000 and decreases again after approximately 7,000 epochs.

rows.subject: MLP5
rows.size_stated: Four hidden layers with 2048, 1024, 512, and 512 neurons; output layer with 10 neurons.
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated test loss over training epochs.
rows.value: The paper reports that test loss did not increase and that MLP5 did not show epoch-wise double descent.
rows.note: Numeric curve values are not stated.
rows.check: State is correct: the paper says MLP5 showed no increase in test loss, only stagnation, so there was no double descent. The 'baseline not stated' field could note that the comparison is with MLP7 under the same setup.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2; Section 3, Figure 1 and accompanying paragraphs: MLP5 trains for 10^6 epochs, shows test-loss stagnation without an increase, and does not exhibit double descent.

rows.subject: MLP3
rows.size_stated: Two hidden layers with 1024 and 512 neurons; output layer with 10 neurons.
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated test loss over training epochs.
rows.value: The paper reports an increase in test loss due to overfitting and states that MLP3 did not show epoch-wise double descent.
rows.note: Numeric curve values are not stated.
rows.check: State is correct for double descent: test loss rose from overfitting with no second descent within 10^6 epochs. The authors classify this as the small-model regime consistent with Nakkiran et al.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2; Section 3, Figure 1 and accompanying paragraphs: MLP3 trains for 10^6 epochs, exhibits increased test loss from overfitting, and does not exhibit double descent.

relation.reason: Its own training trajectories directly test V2, showing epoch-wise double descent in MLP7 and its absence in MLP5 and MLP3.

tranche.reason: The study follows the cited noisy CIFAR-10 setup but uses fully connected MLPs and analyzes epoch-wise test loss and internal activations to investigate the same phenomenon.

source_check.notes: Depth and layer widths vary together, so these comparisons do not isolate depth. Reported error bars concern activation variability across classes or samples, not repeated-run uncertainty in the loss trajectories.
